page: OVHcloud r3-32 is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth tests (both small and large block reads and writes) fall within the average range. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in static web serving throughput and prompt processing for medium-sized (7B) language models, which both rank in the bottom 25%.

The r3-32 instance offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-density multi-threaded compute. With dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per core, it is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-bound text processing tasks. It is less optimal for high-throughput web serving or heavy LLM inference due to its lower network baseline and moderate multi-core scaling.
